recipes.name: Pumpkin Apple Streusel Muffins
ingredients_raw: 2 cups peeled, cored and chopped apple

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease 18 muffin cups or line cups with paper liners.

Sift 2 ½ cups flour, 2 cups sugar, pumpkin pie spice, baking soda, and salt together into a bowl. Combine pumpkin purée, oil, and eggs in a separate bowl; stir into flour mixture until batter is just moistened. Fold in apples.
Divide batter among the prepared muffin cups, filling each to the top.

Whisk remaining ¼ cup sugar, 2 tablespoons flour, and cinnamon together in a bowl; cut in butter with 2 knives or a pastry blender until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Sprinkle cinnamon topping evenly over muffin batter.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into muffins comes out clean, 35 to 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Pumpkin Apple Streusel Muffins
raw_recipe.description: This pumpkin apple streusel muffin recipe features the texture of apples with the warm taste of pumpkin, while the streusel topping adds extra sweetness.

review.reviewBody: Bed & Breakfast quality - moist, tender and sweet! I followed recipe as written. Be sure to allow 30 minutes prep time. Also, if you do not have the 1 Tbls. pumpkin pie spice, substitute: 1 1/2 t. cinnamon, 3/4 t. ginger, scant 1/2 t. allspice, scant 1/2 t. nutmeg.

Don’t use the streusel topping. The muffins are already very sweet. In fact, I may cut ½ cup of the sugar out next time. But they were great and everybody at work gobbled them up. I used all whole wheat flour instead of all-purpose flour and I also used a full can of pumpkin puree because I didn’t want to waste any. I used ½ cup applesauce instead of ½ cup vegetable oil. I didn't have any pumpkin pie spice so I used 2 tsp. cinnamon, ½ tsp. ginger, and ½ tsp. nutmeg as one review suggested. The end result was fantastic!

I read the reviews first. Used some suggestions. First these muffins are done in my oven in 25min. I imagine if I had used the suggested time they would have been dry and overly brown. I did sub brown sugar for the white as I tend to do that with alot of my baking. I have a family of 6 and had my nephews over so I doubled the batch and quadrupled the topping. I used a 3tbl spoon cookie scoop and made overflowing scoops. I got 24 muffins and put the rest in a 9in round pan. The 9in took around 35min to bake. I also don't use pumpkin pie spice so I did a tbl spoon of cinnamon, and a 1/2 tsp of ginger, nutmeg, cloves, and allspice. Everyone loved them. Definitely will use again. Thanks for the great recipe!

The first time I followed the instructions and it came out very well. The second time I added a Tbsp of Vanilla extract to the wet mixture and I chopped and roasted in a single layer 1-Cup of Walnuts at 350 Degrees for 15 mins stirring twice at 5 mins and 10 mins while roasting. The cookie sheet was ling with foil for easy clean-up of the nuts. I let the nuts completely cool before adding them in to the batter. The third time I tried Pecans also roasted and they go very well with this recipe. The fourth time I switched out the Sugar for Splenda for Baking Sweetner in the same amounts. The Splenda amounts could be reduced slightly since the muffins tasted sweeter with the Splenda. How much depends on your tastes.

I altered it because I had a few ingredients that needed to be used up and I also wanted to see if I could make a muffin that would be equally tasty and satisfy my families need to feel full after eating just one muffin. The orginal recipe was a great guide. I did not use the topping just the muffin batter. Love the flavor, a good recipe for sure. 

The changes I made are indicated by an * symbol.

~~~
* 2 cups all-purpose flour
* 1/2 cup powdered peanuts
[Find it where peanut butter is typically located in your store. It tends to keeps you fuller and I did not taste it in my final baked muffin batch.]
* 1 cup brown sugar (I didn't have white sugar)
- 1 tablespoon Pumpkin pie spice 
- 1 teaspoon baking soda
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon 
- 2 eggs, lightly beaten
- 1 cup pumpkin puree 
* 1 apple, w/o skin, core removed graded though 
* A half-cut Zucchini w/o skin, graded through 
* 2 med-sized carrots (not thick), graded through

Damp out with a towel all the moisture from the food gratings. I suggest you have them all in one bowl.

Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Grease or use paper liners.

Use two bowls- one for primary all the 'wets' and another for all the 'dry' ingredients. The food gratings bowl ought to be your 'wet' assigned bowl.

Once you have all your measured ingredients.. pour the 'wets' bowl into the 'dry' one and fold in with a spoon. Fold until it becomes batter-like.

Use spoon to place batter into the muffin tin.

I halved the recipe because I only have one muffin pan. I still used 2 eggs because they were small. I used olive oil instead of vegetable oil. I dusted the tops with cinnamon and sugar instead of the streusel. The muffins were excellent. I will try again with the streusel and also try with a cream cheese light drizzle. I think this is a recipe I will use again and again.

Made this in a bundt pan and added Crasins for a mire festive look. Baked it at 375’F for 45 mins with 10 mins cooling in the oven. I did reduce the sugar by a half cup and replaced it with more pumpkin. Also used 50/50 unsalted butter/veg. oil to give mire substance to the batter since I’m making this into a cake instead of muffins. Instead of the crumbled topping, I dusted it with icing sugar The cake was moist, moderately sweet, and the flavour was mild tasting. Glad I added the half cup of dry cranberries as it gave the cake a bit more flavour. Will give it another try for our Christmas lunch, but will add a tsp of cinnamon to boost the flavours.

I loved these! I'm so thankful to other reviewers who give great advice on recipes. Here are the adjustments I made: I used half & half all-purpose flour and whole wheat flour. I cut the sugar down to 3/4 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup brown sugar. I made the muffins extra big, so my yield was only 11, but I always think bigger is better! 

I'm never sure which apples to use when baking, so I chose honeycrisp. They were perfect.

I did not do the streusel topping but instead made a drizzle for the top. The drizzle consisted of 1 cup of icing sugar, 1/2 tsp. vanilla extract, 1 tbsp. of melted butter, and 1-2 tbsp. of milk (add slowly until you get the desired consistency).

Mmmmmmmarvelous!!

I made bread from this recipe. I used home made pumpkin and I used the cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, and ginger instead of the pumpkin spice. I also used half white sugar and half brown sugar. I didn't have fresh apples, so I used can of stewed apples from my pantry, and I added about a half cup of roasted chopped pecans. I baked two loafs at 325 degrees for an hour and the bread is moist and delicious. I like this recipe because substitutions can be used and it does not effect the outcome of the texture. I didn't use the streusel topping, I just sprinkled sugar over the top of the batter before baking. I will keep this recipe close.

These were delicious! When I saw 2 cups of sugar, I was turned off, but tried the recipe anyway, substituting brown sugar for 1/2 the amount and using whole wheat flour for one cup and white flour for the other one and half cups. I like walnuts in muffins so I added about 1/2 cup finely chopped walnuts. The recipe made 18 muffins, filling the cups to 2/3 full. The streusel is just enough for all 18 and sets off the flavor deliciously. Also, I changed the pumpkin pie spice to 2 tsp pumpkin pie spice and 1 tsp cinnamon. Bake time was a little less. I checked them at 30 min. and they were done, using toothpick method.

Used all white whole wheat flour. Used 1 cup unsweetened applesauce instead of oil and only had 3/4 cup of pumpkin purée. Used brown sugar rather than white and 1/2 what recipe called for. Added 1 cup chopped walnuts. Baked for about 25 min.

Made some with and some without the streusel-- for appearance the streusel just looks prettier. I used 1/2c less sugar and used part brown and part white sugar. Next time I would grate the apple rather than chop. Baked for 30min.
I followed suggestions and used less sugar. I also think the strudel topping is good. I think the recipe is not for 4 teaspoons of butter in the topping? I used 4 Tablespoons.
I made these per the recipe and they were delicious! Now, I’ll try some suggestions to reduce sugar and add whole wheat flour. Great recipe.
I've made this recipe several times- my family and husband's coworkers LOVE this recipe! Definitely a favorite!

I used half oil, half applesauce and didn’t quite have enough pumpkin spice, so added a bunch of the other spices to make up for it. I’d even add more spice to them as I like pumpkin muffins with lots of spice. I used two apples, cut up, which worked ok, though I didn’t measure whether that was 2cups. I might reduce the amount of sugar next time also. I didn’t make the streusel topping this time though I have in the past and didn’t find it worth my time for my tastes. They were just as good without. Second time making it, I reduce sugar by half. That was great. I added a cup of chopped roasted walnuts. Wouldn’t that again! Accidentally added less apple and didn’t chop them enough. Won’t do that again! It made 12muffins that way. They baked waaaay faster than 35mins. Maybe 25 or even 20mins. Turned out a bit dry.

So yum!!! I made some changes, based on what I had on hand and my preferences. But these turned out moist, fluffy and totally sweet enough, even though I cut the sugar in half (used 1 cup) and did not add the topping. Changes: cut sugar in half, did not add topping, used homemade squash puree because I had a bunch of cooked squash leftovers, DOUBLED the amount of squash to make the batter more moist, subbed coconut oil for veg oil because that's what I had. Recommend!
I double this recipe every time I make it and they are gone within 2 days!! My family loves these muffins! Definitely a favorite 😍
Love these muffins!! I may add extra apple pieces next time. I did a 1/2 cup of chopped pecans to the batter, and used cinnamon sugar topping rather than the struesal topping.
